text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY

- President Boris Yeltsin in his radio address on Thursday assured Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin that his position as head of the government was secure and that his two younger first deputies were not trying to step into Chernomyrdin's shoes.
- Russia's Central Bank cut its refinancing rate on Thursday, showing it is confident inflation will continue to slow.

- First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov's appointment to head the Fuel and Energy Ministry will give him a chance to use the ministry's apparatus to help him generate new ideas and prepare documents.
- The tax police promise to be tougher with tax dodgers and widely use the right to take them into custody during investigation.
- Russian tax authorities are going to toughen their stance on foreign companies operating in Russia and avoiding obligatory tax payments.
- FGI Wireless, the biggest foreign shareholder in Russian cellular phone company Vympelkom, is selling its stake in the company.
- Russians, once hit by pyramid scheme companies, balk at mutual funds.
- Shareholders of Ak Bars bank, the biggest commercial bank in Tatarstan, sack its chairman Talgat Abdullin and appoint First Deputy Finance Minister Rinat Gubaidullin to take over.
- The municipality of St Petersburg is drafting a document which will allow companies to pay city taxes in own equity.
- Russia's Central Bank is planning to shift to on-line dealing and clearing operations in 1998.
SEVODNYA
- An announced complete overhaul of the Moscow Customs Committee could mean that somebody just wants to delete the old database from its computers.
- At least 15 companies with big backlogs of overdue tax payments will have to face the Extraordinary Commission on tax arrears in May.
- Foreign companies operating in Russia but registered offshore are among the biggest tax dodgers, says a tax service official at a news conference.
- Account holders in Russian commercial banks are going to be the hardest hit when interest rates go down in the wake of the Central Bank's decision to cut its refinancing rate.
- Russian atomic energy ministry is looking into an option to set up a stock of enriched uranium in the U.S.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Russia has to set up a stock of its uranium in the U.S. for future sales if it is to stay on the market, says Atomic Energy Minister Viktor Mikhailov.
- Belarussian economy is developed enough not to weigh down on Russia when the two countries form union, says Russian Deputy Prime Minister Valery Serov in an article.
- Deputy Prime Minister Yakov Urinson says Rosvooruzheniye will lose its monopoly on Russian arms sales abroad.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov takes over as Fuel and Energy Minister.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- The idea to replace all foreign-made cars used by officials with domestic brands, promoted by First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov, will cost the budget billions of roubles.
--Andrei Shukshin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
